outcome.question: quick one — is 2 min of sparging enough before we drop the catalyst in? thats what the old sop said
outcome.answer:
I need to search the knowledge graph for context on your process — the step, the solvent system, the reaction conditions, and what the evidence actually says about sparging time.I found a reference to degassing in the knowledge graph. Let me pull the full playbook note:**No, 2 minutes is not enough.** The record is explicit: [[playbook-degassing]] states that **"sparging for two minutes is the same as not degassing."**

The standard is **20 minutes per 100 mL of solvent**, or alternatively three freeze-pump-thaw cycles. The playbook was distilled from the Suzuki optimization campaign ([[opt-suzuki-conditions]]) and directly supersedes an older SOP that recommended exactly the 2-minute procedure.

The reason: Pd(0) catalyst is oxidised by dissolved oxygen to inactive black precipitate. A bimodal yield distribution — some runs hitting 70%+ and others crashing below 20% on nominally identical conditions — is the signature that catalyst is randomly dying in the first minutes. That variability only stops when you degas properly.

If your SOP says 2 minutes, it needs updating. What solvent volume are you typically running with?
